metadata.title: Sentinel plan of action and milestones

risks.title: Host STIG baseline not verified by a scan
risks.description: The STIG role applies 55 of the 194 rules in Canonical Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Security Technical Implementation Guide V1R6; 25 are documented deviations and 8 are not applicable. No scan results were supplied, so none of this is verified on a host, and the remaining 106 rules are unassessed.
risks.statement: Host hardening is configured as code but not yet shown to be in effect.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Run deploy/ansible/roles/stig with its scan enabled, convert the results to a checklist with the MITRE SAF CLI, and pass the XCCDF results to the generator (--xccdf).

risks.title: AC-2 (Sentinel node software): planned
risks.description: Put an authenticating proxy (OIDC, or mTLS with CAC/PIV) in front of every node that sets X-Sentinel-Operator from the verified identity and strips any client-supplied value; manage operator accounts in the organization's identity provider. The current Caddyfile does neither.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as planned: The node has no user accounts. It records the operator identity that the front proxy asserts in the X-Sentinel-Operator header (sentinel/api/identity.py) and does not authenticate it.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Put an authenticating proxy (OIDC, or mTLS with CAC/PIV) in front of every node that sets X-Sentinel-Operator from the verified identity and strips any client-supplied value; manage operator accounts in the organization's identity provider. The current Caddyfile does neither.

risks.title: AC-2 (Node host (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS)): partial
risks.description: Apply the STIG role to the hub and verify it with the OpenSCAP scan (stig_scan: true).
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: The installer creates a system account, sentinel, with no login shell, and the service runs as it (deploy/bundle/install.sh, deploy/systemd/sentinel.service). Root cannot log in over SSH (baseline role) or directly (STIG role, UBTU-24-400110); accounts are disabled 35 days after password expiry (UBTU-24-200260); each account is limited to 10 sessions (UBTU-24-200000); changes to account files are audited (UBTU-24-200280 to UBTU-24-200320).

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Apply the STIG role to the hub and verify it with the OpenSCAP scan (stig_scan: true).

risks.title: AC-3 (Sentinel node software): partial
risks.description: Test the read-only refusal on the decision, note and annotation endpoints; authorize by role once operators are authenticated (IA-2), for example so that only a designated role may record a MANEUVER decision or resolve a conflict.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: A read-only node (SENTINEL_READ_ONLY, set on the public hub) answers reads and refuses writes with 403: CDM ingest and AI draft confirmation are tested; the decision, note and annotation endpoints call the same guard (sentinel/api/app.py). A replica merges decision-log entries only from nodes in its trust store; others are rejected before merge and recorded. There is no per-operator authorization: any identity the proxy asserts may write.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Test the read-only refusal on the decision, note and annotation endpoints; authorize by role once operators are authenticated (IA-2), for example so that only a designated role may record a MANEUVER decision or resolve a conflict.

risks.title: AC-3 (Node host (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS)): partial

risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: The service runs sandboxed by systemd: read-only filesystem except its own var directory, no new privileges, no capabilities, restricted address families and system calls, UMask 0077. The node's signing key is written readable only by its owner (mode 0600, sentinel/crdt/signing.py). AppArmor is installed and enabled (STIG role, UBTU-24-100500, UBTU-24-100510).

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Verify the sandbox on a deployed host (systemd-analyze security) and apply the STIG role.

risks.description: Forward the structured logs and audit records to a collector when the link allows, and alert on a failed chain verification instead of reporting it only when asked.

risks.title: AU-9 (Sentinel node software): partial
risks.description: Anchor the AI audit chain's head outside the file (in the signed decision log, or at the hub on reconnect) so truncation is detectable, and alert on a failed verification.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: The AI audit log is hash-chained: editing or deleting a line is detected at that line. Decision-log entries are Ed25519-signed and hash-chained per node; a tampered entry is rejected before merge, and a replica that sees one dot with two different contents stops rather than choose. A decision made offline at an edge arrives at the hub with a valid signature. Truncating the newest lines of the AI audit log leaves a shorter chain that still verifies.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Anchor the AI audit chain's head outside the file (in the signed decision log, or at the hub on reconnect) so truncation is detectable, and alert on a failed verification.

risks.title: AU-10 (Sentinel node software): partial
risks.description: Bind each entry to an authenticated operator (IA-2), for example with a per-operator signature from a CAC/PIV key alongside the node's.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: Every decision-log entry is signed with its authoring node's Ed25519 key and verified against the trust store on merge, so no node can alter another's entries or author entries in its name. A confirmed AI draft carries its provenance: router, confidence, model and the audit sequence of the question. The operator identity inside an entry is asserted by the proxy, not authenticated, so non-repudiation holds for the node, not yet for the person.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Bind each entry to an authenticated operator (IA-2), for example with a per-operator signature from a CAC/PIV key alongside the node's.

risks.title: CM-8 (Build, test and release pipeline): partial
risks.description: Catalogue each container image archive with syft in the release workflow and gate it like the bundle SBOMs. Push the first release tag, then check that the published SBOMs and their attestations match the bundles (gh attestation verify --predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3).
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: Software components are inventoried with versions and hashes. On every push the supply-chain CI job writes SPDX 2.3 and CycloneDX SBOMs with the pinned syft for what a bundle ships from source: the Python runtime (the hash-locked runtime set and the sentinel wheel, installed for the bundle's CPython 3.12 target) and the web console (the production closure of web/package-lock.json). The step fails if an SBOM is empty or lacks a component known to ship (scripts/sbom.py, step "SBOMs (fails if empty or missing a shipped component)"). The bundle builder writes BUNDLE.json, which lists every wheel with its digest and every bundled binary with its version, upstream URL and SHA-256, and refuses a binary with no pin for the target architecture; deploy/tools.lock pins every third-party binary for both architectures. Two gaps remain. The container image's base layer (Chainguard's CPython image) is in no SBOM that Sentinel produces. The airgap-install CI job builds a bundle for each architecture on every push and installs it offline, but SBOMs are published with a release and attested to it only by .github/workflows/release.yml, which runs on a tag on GitHub, has been checked only statically (actionlint) and has not run yet.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Catalogue each container image archive with syft in the release workflow and gate it like the bundle SBOMs. Push the first release tag, then check that the published SBOMs and their attestations match the bundles (gh attestation verify --predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3).

risks.title: CM-14 (Build, test and release pipeline): partial
risks.description: Push the first release tag and confirm that the sign job's offline verification and the verify job (keyless signature, install and run under unshare -rn) pass on both architectures.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: Installation refuses a bundle whose signature does not verify against the approved signer. One verifier, deploy/bundle/verify_signature.sh, holds the policy for every install path. It accepts exactly one policy: the release workflow's keyless identity, checked offline against the Sigstore trusted root (whose SHA-256 is pinned), or a site public key. No policy, two policies, a missing signature bundle, or a trusted root that does not match its pin is refused before cosign runs, and a rejected signature fails closed. On every push the supply-chain CI job runs the verifier with the pinned cosign in a namespace with no network: a good signature verifies; a tampered artifact, another key's signature and a wrong identity are rejected; a real Sigstore public-good signature verifies offline (deploy/bundle/selftest_signature.sh). The same job runs the Ansible role's gate on localhost (deploy/ansible/tests/test_verify.sh): a tampered bundle with a regenerated digest, a missing policy and another signer's identity are refused. The airgap-install CI job runs the full offline install behind the gate on every push, for each architecture (make airgap-local): it builds a bundle, signs it with a throwaway key, and in a namespace with no network verifies that signature before unpacking, installs and runs the node. Not yet proven: releases are signed keyless only by the sign job of .github/workflows/release.yml, which runs on a tag on GitHub, has been checked only statically (actionlint) and has not run yet, so no Sentinel release signature exists, and the full install is exercised on every push only in key mode, not against the release workflow's keyless identity. Unpacking a bundle by hand and running install.sh skips the gate by construction: a script inside a bundle cannot vouch for that bundle.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Push the first release tag and confirm that the sign job's offline verification and the verify job (keyless signature, install and run under unshare -rn) pass on both architectures.

risks.title: RA-5 (Build, test and release pipeline): partial
risks.description: Run the vulnerability gate daily as well as on every push; gate the container image scan once base-image findings have a VEX process; run the STIG scan on the hub.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: On every push the supply-chain CI job scans with the pinned Trivy against its current vulnerability database, which is not pinned. It scans uv.lock (every locked package, dev tools and optional extras included), the console's runtime dependencies in web/package-lock.json, and the nats-server and uv binaries the bundle ships, for both architectures. Every reviewed VEX statement must answer a finding the raw scan reported and pass its evidence check against the shipped binaries, and a not_affected statement must carry an OpenVEX justification and a written impact statement. Then any finding left, at any severity, fails the job, with an exit code distinct from Trivy's own errors (scripts/scan.py, step "Vulnerability gate (raw scan, reviewed VEX and its evidence checked, SARIF)"). Secret scanning (gitleaks) runs over the full history on every push. Not yet covered: no scan runs on a schedule, so a new advisory against unchanged code is found only on the next push; the container image is scanned only in release.yml, which has not run yet, and its findings are reported, not gated; the npm build toolchain (devDependencies) is not scanned; and host compliance scanning with OpenSCAP against the DISA STIG benchmark is defined in the STIG role but has not been run. When it is, its failing rules become POA&M items automatically.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Run the vulnerability gate daily as well as on every push; gate the container image scan once base-image findings have a VEX process; run the STIG scan on the hub.

risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: Every failing test becomes a POA&M item, linked to the controls that cite it, on every CI run (this package). A dependency update reaches CI only as a change to uv.lock, because the jobs that test install exactly the lock (uv sync --locked, which a test requires), so the full test ladder runs on the update itself. On every push the vulnerability gate fails the build on any finding in a dependency or a shipped binary that no reviewed VEX statement answers (RA-5), so a known flaw cannot pass unnoticed. Those findings reach the job's SARIF output, not yet this package's POA&M.

risks.title: SI-7 (Node host (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS)): partial
risks.description: Apply the STIG role to the hub and scan. Push the first release tag and confirm that the release workflow's verify job passes on keyless-signed bundles.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: Installation verifies before it unpacks, and each check fails closed. The sentinel Ansible role first verifies the bundle's signature on the target (verify.yml: the pinned cosign, itself checked against deploy/tools.lock on the host, runs verify_signature.sh), then the tarball's SHA-256; install.sh then checks every file against the bundle's SHA256SUMS and installs dependencies offline with --require-hashes. CI exercises the signature gate on every push: on localhost, a tampered bundle is refused even when its .sha256 is regenerated to match (deploy/ansible/tests/test_verify.sh, in the supply-chain job). The complete offline path (deploy/bundle/verify_offline.sh: signature, digest, SHA256SUMS, install and run inside unshare -rn) runs on every push in the airgap-install CI job, on a freshly built bundle for each architecture signed with a throwaway key (make airgap-local); the bundle's SHA256SUMS covers the reference data it ships. The release workflow runs the same path on keyless-signed bundles and has not run yet. AIDE checks file integrity daily (STIG role), and the STIG role has not been applied to a host.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Apply the STIG role to the hub and scan. Push the first release tag and confirm that the release workflow's verify job passes on keyless-signed bundles.

risks.title: SI-7 (Build, test and release pipeline): partial
risks.description: Push the first release tag; confirm the sign job's offline verification passes, then verify the published release offline as docs/supply-chain.md describes.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: The release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml, sign job) signs every release artifact keyless: both bundles, both container image archives, and SHA256SUMS, which covers the SBOMs, the VEX document and the trusted root. Before anything is uploaded it verifies every signature offline under unshare -rn against the pinned trusted root and the exact workflow identity, and it attests SLSA build provenance. That workflow runs only on a tag on GitHub. It has been checked statically (actionlint with shellcheck, in the release-lint CI job) and has not run yet, so no release has been signed. The verifier it calls is exercised on every push with the real cosign and no network (deploy/bundle/selftest_signature.sh, in the supply-chain CI job).

risks.title: SR-3 (Build, test and release pipeline): partial
risks.description: Push the first release tag so that signing, provenance and SBOM attestation run.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: The supply-chain controls are documented in docs/supply-chain.md, and the supply-chain CI job runs them on every push: SBOMs with a completeness gate (CM-8), a Trivy scan that fails on any finding no reviewed VEX statement answers (RA-5), and offline signature verification with the real cosign (CM-14, SI-7). Third-party binaries and trust material are pinned by version and SHA-256 (deploy/tools.lock); a mismatch writes nothing (scripts/fetch_tools.py, used by every job that fetches a tool). Python dependencies are hash-locked in uv.lock. The CI jobs that test and assess install exactly the lock with uv sync --locked, which refuses a stale lock, and a test fails any workflow that installs with pip or uv pip instead, since those resolve afresh; a bundle installs them offline with --require-hashes. Upstream data (NASA CARA, CelesTrak, NIST, DISA) is vendored unmodified with provenance and checksums that the tests verify. Every action in every workflow is pinned by commit SHA, which a test enforces (tests/test_workflows_pinned.py). Not yet done: signing, SLSA provenance and SBOM attestation of releases exist only in release.yml, which has not run yet.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Push the first release tag so that signing, provenance and SBOM attestation run.

risks.title: SR-4 (Build, test and release pipeline): partial
risks.description: Push the first release tag; verify the published provenance and SBOM attestations online (gh attestation verify) and offline (cosign verify-blob-attestation against the pinned trusted root), as docs/supply-chain.md describes. Build L3 needs the provenance generated in an isolated, trusted reusable workflow.
risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: Provenance is recorded for vendored upstream data (fixtures/cara/PROVENANCE.md, fixtures/omm/PROVENANCE.md, compliance/vendor/nist/PROVENANCE.md, compliance/vendor/disa/PROVENANCE.md) and each NASA CARA test case documents its source and tolerance. Each bundle's BUNDLE.json records the commit it was built from, whether that tree was clean or dirty, its SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, and the upstream URL and SHA-256 of every bundled binary; a build from uncommitted changes cannot pass as its commit. deploy/tools.lock records the upstream URL and SHA-256 of every third-party binary, and uv.lock the registry, file URL and SHA-256 of every third-party Python distribution; the CI jobs that test and assess install exactly what uv.lock records (uv sync --locked), which a test requires. SLSA v1 build provenance (Build L2) and SBOM attestations for every tarball and image archive are generated by the sign job of .github/workflows/release.yml and shipped as files, so they verify offline. That workflow runs only on a tag on GitHub, has been checked only statically (actionlint) and has not run yet, so no release provenance exists. Build L3 is not claimed: the provenance is generated inside this repository's own workflow (docs/supply-chain.md).

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Push the first release tag; verify the published provenance and SBOM attestations online (gh attestation verify) and offline (cosign verify-blob-attestation against the pinned trusted root), as docs/supply-chain.md describes. Build L3 needs the provenance generated in an isolated, trusted reusable workflow.

risks.statement: Stated in the SSP as partial: A component is refused unless it is what was pinned. Downloaded tools and the Sigstore trusted root are accepted only if their SHA-256 matches deploy/tools.lock, and a mismatch writes nothing (scripts/fetch_tools.py). Sentinel's own bundles are refused unless their cosign signature verifies against the approved signer, and the trusted root is checked against its pin before use; the supply-chain CI job exercises both with the real cosign and no network on every push. The Ansible role re-checks the cosign binary's SHA-256 on the target host before running it. The container base images are pinned by registry digest (deploy/containers/Dockerfile), and every workflow action by commit SHA (tests/test_workflows_pinned.py). Not yet done: APT on the host refuses unauthenticated packages only once the STIG role, not yet applied, has run.

risks.title: STIG deviation: SSH shows the exercise notice, not the DoD Notice and Consent Banner
risks.description: The public demonstration node is not a U.S. Government information system. Presenting the USG notice there would misrepresent the system to anyone who connects.
risks.statement: 2 STIG rules are not met by design: UBTU-24-200640, UBTU-24-200680.

mitigating-factors.description: The mechanism is in place: sshd's Banner directive is set, and the node shows an UNCLASSIFIED // EXERCISE authorized-use notice (deploy/ansible/roles/baseline). The DoD text and the acknowledgement prompt are in the role, verbatim from the STIG, behind stig_dod_banner.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Set stig_dod_banner: true on any deployment that is a U.S. Government information system.

risks.title: STIG deviation: Only SSH is rate-limited by the host firewall
risks.description: ufw's LIMIT denies a source address after six new connections in thirty seconds. Operators behind one NAT address would share that budget for the console on 443, and an edge's NATS leafnode reconnects every second after a drop (deploy/nats/edge.conf.tmpl, reconnect 1s), so limiting 7422 would block an edge exactly while it recovers from a DDIL outage: the behaviour the RECOVERY harness scenario exists to protect.
risks.statement: 1 STIG rule is not met by design: UBTU-24-600200.

mitigating-factors.description: SSH (22) is rate-limited. 7422 accepts only allow-listed edge networks, in ufw (stig_leaf_allowed_cidrs) and in the AWS security group (leaf_allowed_cidrs, empty by default so the port is closed). 443 is served by Caddy in front of a read-only node.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Replace host-level rate limiting on 443 with request limits at the proxy, sized from measured console behaviour, and document the leafnode port's reconnect profile with the ISSO.

risks.title: STIG deviation: The host does not run in FIPS mode
risks.description: FIPS mode needs Ubuntu Pro's FIPS-certified kernel and modules, which the demonstration hub does not carry. Sentinel's own signatures (Ed25519, via the Python cryptography package's bundled OpenSSL) do not use a FIPS-validated module either.
risks.statement: 1 STIG rule is not met by design: UBTU-24-600030.

mitigating-factors.description: SSH is restricted to the STIG's FIPS 140-3 approved ciphers, MACs and key exchange algorithms (UBTU-24-100820, UBTU-24-100830, UBTU-24-100840, applied).

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Build the node image with Ubuntu Pro fips-updates, and move Sentinel's signing to a FIPS-validated provider (SC-13 in the SSP).

risks.title: STIG deviation: No CAC/PIV logon and no DoD PKI certificate authorities
risks.description: PKI-based multifactor logon needs a DoD PKI (CAC/PIV cards, DoD root CAs, OCSP or CRLs) that the demonstration environment does not have.

mitigating-factors.description: Administrative access is SSH public-key only (password and keyboard-interactive authentication off, root login off), from the admin_cidr network only; the AWS variable rejects 0.0.0.0/0. Session Manager is the break-glass path.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: On a DoD network: SSSD with pam_pkcs11 for CAC/PIV logon, the DoD root CAs as the trust anchors, and a local revocation cache for disconnected operation (IA-2 in the SSP).

risks.title: STIG deviation: The automation account escalates without a password
risks.description: The Ubuntu cloud image's default account has NOPASSWD sudo (/etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users), and the Ansible playbook depends on it to become root.
risks.statement: 1 STIG rule is not met by design: UBTU-24-300020.

mitigating-factors.description: The account is reachable only by SSH public key from the admin network; every sudo use is audited (UBTU-24-900170, applied).

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Give Ansible a become password from a vault, or document the account with the ISSO as an administrative group using MFA, as the rule allows.

risks.title: STIG deviation: Data at rest is encrypted by the platform, not by the operating system
risks.description: The hub's root volume is encrypted by EBS (deploy/aws/terraform/main.tf, encrypted = true), which the operating-system check (every partition in /etc/crypttab) cannot see.
risks.statement: 1 STIG rule is not met by design: UBTU-24-600090.

mitigating-factors.description: EBS encryption with AWS-managed keys covers the hub's only volume.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Edge hardware is provisioned with LUKS full-disk encryption, set up at install time (SC-28 in the SSP).

risks.title: STIG deviation: No boot-loader password
risks.description: The hub runs on EC2, where there is no interactive boot console unless EC2 serial console access is enabled, and the Terraform does not enable it.
risks.statement: 1 STIG rule is not met by design: UBTU-24-102000.

mitigating-factors.description: Console access to the instance is not configured; administration is SSH and Session Manager.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Set a GRUB superuser password, from a managed secret, when edge hardware is provisioned.

risks.title: STIG deviation: Audit records stay on the node
risks.description: There is no central audit collector in this deployment, and an edge node cannot reach one while its link is denied, which is the condition Sentinel is designed for.
risks.statement: 2 STIG rules are not met by design: UBTU-24-100450, UBTU-24-900950.

mitigating-factors.description: Audit rules are immutable once loaded (UBTU-24-909000); Sentinel's own decision log is signed and hash-chained per node and replicates to the hub when the link returns.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Offload with audisp-remote to a collector on reconnect; for a standalone edge, a weekly offload to removable media as UBTU-24-900950 describes.

risks.title: STIG deviation: The default time source is not a DoD authoritative source
risks.description: The AWS hub uses the Amazon Time Sync Service (169.254.169.123), the source it can reach. The role applies the rest of the rule: only the configured sources, polled at least every 24 hours (maxpoll 16), with the Ubuntu pools disabled.
risks.statement: 1 STIG rule is not met by design: UBTU-24-600160.

mitigating-factors.description: Clocks step when more than one second out (UBTU-24-600180, applied) and use UTC (UBTU-24-901220, applied).

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Set stig_time_servers to the enclave's authoritative DoD time source on any DoD deployment.

risks.title: STIG deviation: Audit storage and failure alerts are not mailed to the SA and ISSO
risks.description: The node has no mail transport, and an edge has no route to a mail relay while disconnected.
risks.statement: 2 STIG rules are not met by design: UBTU-24-900960, UBTU-24-900980.

mitigating-factors.description: In upstream auditd 3.1.2's default configuration, low storage is logged to syslog (space_left_action = SYSLOG); a full or failing disk suspends audit logging (SUSPEND). Neither reaches a person, which is why this is a POA&M item.

remediations.title: Planned remediation
remediations.description: Raise audit storage and failure alerts through auditd's exec action into the node's own alerting path, which reaches the operator console locally and the hub when connected.

poam-items.remarks:
UBTU-24-200640 (V-270691, SV-270691r1066562_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must display the Standard Mandatory DOD Notice and Consent Banner before granting access to via an SSH logon.
UBTU-24-200680 (V-270694, SV-270694r1066571_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must be configured to enforce the acknowledgement of the Standard Mandatory DOD Notice and Consent Banner for all SSH connections.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: Only SSH is rate-limited by the host firewall
poam-items.description: ufw's LIMIT denies a source address after six new connections in thirty seconds. Operators behind one NAT address would share that budget for the console on 443, and an edge's NATS leafnode reconnects every second after a drop (deploy/nats/edge.conf.tmpl, reconnect 1s), so limiting 7422 would block an edge exactly while it recovers from a DDIL outage: the behaviour the RECOVERY harness scenario exists to protect.
poam-items.remarks: UBTU-24-600200 (V-270754, SV-270754r1066751_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must configure the uncomplicated firewall to rate-limit impacted network interfaces.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: The host does not run in FIPS mode
poam-items.description: FIPS mode needs Ubuntu Pro's FIPS-certified kernel and modules, which the demonstration hub does not carry. Sentinel's own signatures (Ed25519, via the Python cryptography package's bundled OpenSSL) do not use a FIPS-validated module either.
poam-items.remarks: UBTU-24-600030 (V-270744, SV-270744r1137699_rule, CAT I): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must implement NIST FIPS-validated cryptography to protect classified information and for the following: To provision digital signatures, to generate cryptographic hashes, and to protect unclassified information requiring confidentiality and cryptographic protection in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards.

poam-items.description: PKI-based multifactor logon needs a DoD PKI (CAC/PIV cards, DoD root CAs, OCSP or CRLs) that the demonstration environment does not have.
poam-items.remarks:
UBTU-24-100650 (V-270662, SV-270662r1067156_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must have the "SSSD" package installed.
UBTU-24-100660 (V-270663, SV-270663r1066478_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must use the "SSSD" package for multifactor authentication services.
UBTU-24-100900 (V-270672, SV-270672r1067161_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must accept Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials.
UBTU-24-100910 (V-270673, SV-270673r1067164_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must accept Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials managed through the Privileged Access Management (PAM)  framework.
UBTU-24-400020 (V-270721, SV-270721r1066652_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must implement smart card logins for multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged and nonprivileged accounts.
UBTU-24-400030 (V-270722, SV-270722r1067130_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must implement smart card logins for multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged and nonprivileged accounts over SSH.
UBTU-24-400060 (V-270723, SV-270723r1066658_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must electronically verify Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials.
UBTU-24-400340 (V-270734, SV-270734r1155240_rule, CAT III): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must be configured such that Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) prohibits the use of cached authentications after one day.
UBTU-24-400360 (V-270735, SV-270735r1066694_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, for PKI-based authentication, SSSD must validate certificates by constructing a certification path (which includes status information) to an accepted trust anchor.
UBTU-24-400370 (V-270736, SV-270736r1066697_rule, CAT I): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must map the authenticated identity to the user or group account for PKI-based authentication.
UBTU-24-400375 (V-270737, SV-270737r1067178_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, for PKI-based authentication, Privileged Access Management (PAM) must validate certificates by constructing a certification path (which includes status information) to an accepted trust anchor.
UBTU-24-400380 (V-270738, SV-270738r1066703_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS for PKI-based authentication, must implement a local cache of revocation data in case of the inability to access revocation information via the network.
UBTU-24-600060 (V-270745, SV-270745r1066724_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must use DOD PKI-established certificate authorities (CAs) for verification of the establishment of protected sessions.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: The automation account escalates without a password
poam-items.description: The Ubuntu cloud image's default account has NOPASSWD sudo (/etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users), and the Ansible playbook depends on it to become root.
poam-items.remarks: UBTU-24-300020 (V-274868, SV-274868r1107313_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must require users to provide a password for privilege escalation.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: Data at rest is encrypted by the platform, not by the operating system
poam-items.description: The hub's root volume is encrypted by EBS (deploy/aws/terraform/main.tf, encrypted = true), which the operating-system check (every partition in /etc/crypttab) cannot see.
poam-items.remarks: UBTU-24-600090 (V-270747, SV-270747r1066730_rule, CAT II): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS handling data requiring "data at rest" protections must employ cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of the information at rest.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: No boot-loader password
poam-items.description: The hub runs on EC2, where there is no interactive boot console unless EC2 serial console access is enabled, and the Terraform does not enable it.
poam-items.remarks: UBTU-24-102000 (V-270675, SV-270675r1137691_rule, CAT I): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS when booted must require authentication upon booting into single-user and maintenance modes.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: Audit records stay on the node
poam-items.description: There is no central audit collector in this deployment, and an edge node cannot reach one while its link is denied, which is the condition Sentinel is designed for.
poam-items.remarks:
UBTU-24-100450 (V-270658, SV-270658r1067151_rule, CAT III): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS audit event multiplexor must be configured to offload audit logs onto a different system or storage media from the system being audited.
UBTU-24-900950 (V-270817, SV-270817r1066940_rule, CAT III): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must have a crontab script running weekly to offload audit events of standalone systems.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: The default time source is not a DoD authoritative source
poam-items.description: The AWS hub uses the Amazon Time Sync Service (169.254.169.123), the source it can reach. The role applies the rest of the rule: only the configured sources, polled at least every 24 hours (maxpoll 16), with the Ubuntu pools disabled.
poam-items.remarks: UBTU-24-600160 (V-270751, SV-270751r1066742_rule, CAT III): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must compare internal information system clocks at least every 24 hours with an authoritative time server.

poam-items.title: STIG deviation: Audit storage and failure alerts are not mailed to the SA and ISSO
poam-items.description: The node has no mail transport, and an edge has no route to a mail relay while disconnected.
poam-items.remarks:
UBTU-24-900960 (V-270818, SV-270818r1066943_rule, CAT III): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must immediately notify the system administrator (SA) and information system security officer (ISSO) (at a minimum) when allocated audit record storage volume reaches 75 percent of the repository maximum audit record storage capacity.
UBTU-24-900980 (V-270819, SV-270819r1068390_rule, CAT III): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must alert the system administrator (SA) and information system security officer (ISSO) (at a minimum) in the event of an audit processing failure.
